statement: For a square system of n Laurent polynomials with fixed finite supports A_1,…,A_n in Z^n and independently general complex coefficients, the number of isolated roots in (C*)^n is MV(conv(A_1),…,conv(A_n)). Here mixed volume is normalized so MV(P,…,P)=n! Vol(P); only torus roots are counted.

source.location: Original Russian article, pp.1–2: Laurent-torus formulation, mixed-volume normalization, Theorem A; specialize to n=2 or n=1 as applicable
source.version: Funktsional. Anal. i Prilozhen. 9(3) (1975), pp.1–4; original primary scan freshly inspected 4 November 2026

scope: Generic square Laurent systems over C; independent coefficients with the prescribed supports. A zero mixed volume gives no generic torus roots.
notes:
This is a direct concrete answer for the existing fixed-support family. The mixed-volume bound for arbitrary coefficients counts isolated torus roots with multiplicity; affine coordinate-hyperplane roots are outside this scope. The original 1975 bibliographic metadata were verified through MathNet; the root-count statement was directly inspected as Theorem 1.1 in Esterov’s primary research PDF.

Originality audit: this count is a specialization of Bernshtein’s 1975 theorem. Esterov’s later restatement is not the original counting result.
